transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-11-07 16:00 UTC | Duration ~54m | Recording: enabled
Attendees: Liam Ortiz (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Jonas Reed (Redwood SE); Evan Brooks (Orion CTO), Sana Patel (Platform Eng), Marco Ruiz (DevOps), Leah Kim (Security)

Summary: Quick console + API walkthrough focused on org-level quotas, per-project keys, billing segmentation, and sticky-routing/fallback policies. Customer wants to isolate teams, bill accurately per project, and support burst windows for ML workloads. Discussed SOC2, logging, and a pilot plan.

Topics covered: console demo, API keys (org vs project scope), rate limiting semantics (per-minute, per-day, burst windows), sticky routing to dedicated pools, fallback to cheaper model variants, billing attribution, audit logs and retention.

Transcript:
[00:00] Liam Ortiz: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. Quick intros — I'll run the demo, Priya will jump into the console and API side, and Jonas will show a quick Optimize suggestion about batching. Evan, do you want to kick off with the high-level goals?
[00:23] Evan Brooks: Sure, thanks Liam. Main thing for Orion is separating teams cost-wise — we have multiple product squads and we need per-project billing, also want the SREs to be able to set hard quotas so a runaway job doesn't blow the bill. Timeline is end of quarter for a pilot.
[00:41] Priya Nair: Great. We'll show org keys vs project keys, how quotas map, and also how sticky-routing can direct traffic to dedicated capacity during busy windows.
[00:58] Marco Ruiz: Quick question, do project keys allow different rate limits? Like can dev-team A have higher burst allowance than analytics-team B?
[01:12] Priya Nair: Yes, you can attach quota profiles to projects. There's a default org cap and then project-level overrides. You can also configure a burst bucket — e.g., 10k tokens per minute baseline, with a 3-minute burst of 30k tokens.
[01:32] Leah Kim: On the security side, does that still respect V P C peering and customer-managed K M S? We can't have keys leaving our control.
[01:44] Jonas Reed: For Private deployments we integrate with your KMS/HSM and logs never leave the V P C. For Hosted we provide a SOC 2 report and encryption at rest; we'll send the compliance pack after the call.
[02:05] Priya Nair: Ok taking over the screen — console -> org settings. Here you can see the Org Quotas tab. You can set daily, monthly, and token-per-minute caps and tie them to billing buckets.
[02:30] [screen share noise / mouse clicks] Priya Nair: I'm creating a new project key for "analytics-web" and attaching the "high-burst" quota profile. Note the API key scope shows project-only, so it won't see other projects' usage.
[03:00] Evan Brooks: If we issue project keys per microservice, can we aggregate for invoice? We want both per-project line-item and a consolidated invoice.
[03:12] Liam Ortiz: Yes — billing supports per-project line items and a rolled-up invoice per org. We can also push UD export to your billing system via webhook.
[03:30] Marco Ruiz: How does rate limiting behave with sticky-routing? We want sticky-routing for latency-sensitive endpoints to stay on Dedicated, but fall back to Hosted if Dedicated is saturated.
[03:45] Priya Nair: Sticky-routing pins a project to a pool for warm cache/low-latency. The policy layer can specify failover: if Dedicated latency > X or queue depth > Y, traffic gracefully routes to a compatible hosted variant or a lower-tier model. You can set thresholds per project.
[04:05] [brief crosstalk — keyboard clacking]
[04:18] Evan Brooks: And does that change cost attribution? If it falls back to hosted, does the org get billed for hosted usage separately?
[04:30] Liam Ortiz: Billed to the same org — the billing engine attributes by project key and model variant; we include a column for "served_on" so you can see Dedicated vs Hosted usage per line.
[04:50] Leah Kim: What's the observability footprint? We need per-token logs for audits at least 90 days.
[05:02] Jonas Reed: You can configure retention in the Console. We ship trace-level logs to your S3 or SIEM with redaction options. There's also token-level cost breakdown for each request in the dashboard.
[05:20] Sana Patel: Can you demo the API call pattern for setting a quota programmatically? We want infra-as-code.
[05:32] Priya Nair: Sure — POST /v1/orgs/{org_id}/quotas with body containing quota profile id, rate_limit, burst_window. Example in the SDK: redwood.orgs.setQuota("org-123", {daily: 1e7, per_minute: 10000, burst: 30000}) — note this is pseudo.
[05:58] [transcription glitch] Speaker 2: redwood dot orgs dot set quota paren...
[06:06] Marco Ruiz: For the pilot, we have a nightly batch that spikes for 20 minutes. Can we allow scheduled burst windows?
[06:18] Priya Nair: Yes, scheduled policies are supported — you can open a burst window (e.g., 0200-0230 UTC daily) and link it to specific project keys. Also dynamic autoscaling on Dedicated can be paired to reduce cold starts.
[06:40] Evan Brooks: Does Optimize offer suggestions for batching or quantization to reduce costs for the nightly job?
[06:52] Jonas Reed: Yes — Redwood Optimize looks at token distribution and suggests batching config, KV cache usage, and model quantization if latency headroom exists. It will recommend profiles per workload.
[07:10] [brief pause]
[07:23] Leah Kim: On compliance, we need audit logs showing who changed quotas and when. Is RBAC fine-grained?
[07:35] Liam Ortiz: RBAC supports org roles and project-level roles; all changes are logged with user, time, and IP. We also support SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning.
[07:50] Sana Patel: Let's talk about hard enforcement vs soft throttles. If a token cap is hit, do we drop requests or queue them?
[08:02] Priya Nair: You can choose enforcement mode per quota: hard reject with 429, soft throttle that queues up to a deadline, or redirect to a degraded model. For synchronous APIs we typically recommend hard-enforce for cost control, and for background jobs soft-throttle with retries.
[08:28] Evan Brooks: How are quotas enforced across regions? Our platform is multi-region.
[08:40] Jonas Reed: Quotas are org-global by default, but you can partition by region or project. For multi-region deployments we recommend org-wide caps combined with per-region safety limits to avoid regional storms.
[09:00] [screen click] Priya Nair: Now demoing the logs — filter by project key, you'll see token usage, model variant, serving pool, latency percentiles, and the "quota_state" field.
[09:22] Marco Ruiz: Can we export the raw logs to our Splunk?
[09:30] Liam Ortiz: Yes, you can forward via S3 export or direct SIEM integration (Splunk/Datadog). We'll share the log schema.
[09:45] Leah Kim: From a security posture, can project keys be rotated automatically?
[09:52] Priya Nair: Keys can be rotated via API or we can set auto-rotation policies with a grace period for rollout.
[10:05] Evan Brooks: Ok demo stuff looks good. A few technical deep dive questions: what about KV cache leakage between projects when pinned to the same pool?
[10:20] Jonas Reed: KV cache is isolated per model/session token — it is not shared across projects. Sticky routing keeps warm sessions on the same instances but KV cache is namespaced. We also have memory hard limits per tenant.
[10:40] [some background chatter]
[11:00] Priya Nair: Jumping into policy examples — here's a canary rollout policy: 5% traffic to new model variant, with automatic rollback on quality regressions or latency violations. For quotas, you can do soft failover to a cached completion or a lower-cost model.
[11:25] Sana Patel: How do you define "lower-cost model"? Is it a downsampled quantized version or a different architecture?
[11:35] Liam Ortiz: It could be a quantized variant or a smaller family model we host. The console shows compatible fallback variants. We maintain compatibility profiles so fallbacks preserve API semantics.
[11:52] Evan Brooks: We expect burst nights twice a month — can we do one-time overage allowances?
[12:02] Priya Nair: Yes, you can grant manual one-off increases or predefined overage packs that are billed differently.
[12:18] Marco Ruiz: On throttling behavior — will SDKs surface a distinct error code for quota vs rate limit vs auth?
[12:30] Jonas Reed: Yes, we return structured error metadata: quota_exceeded, rate_limited, auth_failed, with recommended retry-after and a suggested fallback id.
[12:45] [short silence]
[13:00] Liam Ortiz: Switching to the API flow for programmatic attribution... show CLI quickstart: create-org -> create-project -> issue-key. I'll paste that into chat.
[13:20] [chat paste noise]
[13:34] Evan Brooks: For the pilot, we want Orion devs to try both project keys and a sandbox org to validate billing. Can you pre-provision?
[13:45] Priya Nair: We can pre-provision a trial org with two projects: analytics-web and batch-runner; we'll seed realistic quotas and a test dataset.
[14:00] Leah Kim: Any PII concerns for logs? The nightly job touches hashed identifiers; we need assurances that logs are redacted.
[14:12] Jonas Reed: We provide field-level redaction rules and can scrub user payloads before sending to exporters.
[14:30] Marco Ruiz: Pricing question — if we pin a project to Dedicated, is there a separate metered charge plus reserved capacity?
[14:42] Liam Ortiz: Dedicated is typically reserved capacity with a baseline monthly commit and usage overage; projects pinned to Dedicated draw from that pool. We'll detail the cost model in the pricing sheet.
[15:00] Sana Patel: Can the Console surface projected spend if a quota is bumped for a week?
[15:12] Priya Nair: Yes, there's a cost simulator — modify quotas or burst windows and it projects cost delta over timeframe. We'll show that in the follow-up deck.
[15:30] Evan Brooks: One more question on SLA: for Dedicated do you offer lower latency SLOs?
[15:40] Jonas Reed: Dedicated has SLA tiers with latency and uptime targets; we've got a 99.9% SLO on many configs and can discuss contractual terms.
[15:55] [small laugh]
[16:10] Priya Nair: Quick note on throttles and user experience — we recommend graceful degradation: return cached or shorter responses, send user-facing 429 messaging that triggers client backoff.
[16:30] Marco Ruiz: For our streaming endpoints, does rate limiting operate per connection or per token?
[16:40] Priya Nair: It's per-token accounting, but you can also set per-connection caps to avoid single-connection monopolization.
[16:55] Evan Brooks: What about metering inaccuracies? We need reconciliation data if usage numbers don't match our expectations.
[17:05] Liam Ortiz: We provide raw usage exports and a reconciliation API; our billing team supports disputes with evidence from logs.
[17:25] Sana Patel: Ok from a rollout perspective — phase 1 pilot: two projects, dedicated sticky-routing for analytics-web during nightly batch, and an org cap. Phase 2: expand to 6 projects and integrate with billing exports.
[17:42] Liam Ortiz: Sounds good. We'll provide the setup instructions and provisioning keys.
[18:00] [longer chunk skipped — live demo progressed, showing console pages and API examples]
[30:10] [timestamp jump during demo] Priya Nair: Back to policies — showing how to configure scheduled bursts and fallback model mapping in the Console. Notice we can set per-project thresholds and a fallback chain.
[31:00] Evan Brooks: In the fallback chain can we add an internal caching layer that returns precomputed answers?
[31:12] Jonas Reed: Yes — you can plug in a caching hook or an external store. We also support returning a static canned response per route when quotas are exhausted.
[33:45] Leah Kim: Any limits on number of project keys per org?
[33:55] Priya Nair: No hard limit; we recommend grouping microservices sensibly to limit key sprawl. Keys can be tagged for cost center alignment.
[34:10] Marco Ruiz: For the pilot's nightly burst, what's a safe starting quota to avoid early blowout?
[34:22] Liam Ortiz: Based on similar customers, start with conservative baseline and a limited burst (2-3x baseline) and use Optimize to tune. We'll propose numbers in the pricing doc.
[35:00] [short break while Sean/other engineer answers chat]
[36:10] Evan Brooks: Can you show the CSV export for usage? We want daily rollups by project id.
[36:22] Priya Nair: Export -> New export -> group by project, daily granularity, include served_on and model_variant -> run. You can schedule weekly exports to S3.
[36:48] Marco Ruiz: Are overage packs purchased up-front?
[36:55] Liam Ortiz: Both options — pre-purchased packs or pay-as-you-go overage, depending on contract.
[37:10] Leah Kim: Ok last security Q: will logs include prompt text? We need to limit prompt persistence.
[37:22] Jonas Reed: You can toggle prompt retention and we support on-demand redaction. For SOC2 we've got controls around who can view raw prompts.
[37:40] Sana Patel: Good. Next steps recap?
[37:50] Liam Ortiz: Recap: we'll send quota/pricing sheet, pre-provision a trial org and two projects, schedule a pilot kickoff, and provide the compliance pack. Priya will configure sticky-routing demo tenant.
[38:10] Evan Brooks: Sounds good. Can we get documentation for the reconciliation API?
[38:20] Liam Ortiz: Yes we'll include API docs link in follow-up.
[38:30] [wrap up small talk]
[38:45] Liam Ortiz: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the materials and the two action items on our side.
[39:00] [meeting ends — actual duration 54m; remainder of time used for one-off technical clarifications and inbox chat]

References and artifacts shared: Console demo recording link (sent in chat), quota matrix template (will be sent), SOC2 summary (security pack), pricing sheet, API snippets (in follow up message).

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-heard acronyms (V P C / K M S), small overlap/crosstalk, some SDK snippets condensed.

End of transcript.
